# kmtest conformance baseline — parse_kmtest_serial.py format
# arch=i386 smp=2  generated by `vibeos-cli conformance --arch i386 --smp 2 --write-baseline`
# IoInterrupt banks 306 failures ON PURPOSE — they are the MP owner stamp, not slack.
#   IoInterrupt.c's CheckSpinLock asserts a held lock reads EXACTLY 1 when
#   KmtIsMultiProcessorBuild (on MP the word IS the lock), but only non-zero on a UP
#   checked build (there the stamp is a pure diagnostic). Our MP kernel writes
#   KeGetCurrentThread()|1 over it — 0xB0FF0021 in the failure text. That is UPSTREAM
#   ReactOS: the pre-fork 5213cf717cf already puts the interlocked acquire under
#   `#ifdef CONFIG_SMP` and the stamp under a plain `#if DBG`. Benign for exclusion
#   (bit 0 is set either way; release is an unconditional InterlockedAnd(...,0)), and
#   ntkrnl-sys KxAcquireSpinLock's SPIN_LOCK_ALREADY_OWNED detector READS this stamp —
#   removing it to satisfy the assertion would disarm the instrument hunting the
#   arm64 --smp 1 stall. Owed: make MP store 1 and track the owner out-of-band.
#   Re-seeded 2026-08-02; every row below agreed across THREE independent boots.
#   IoDeviceObject (both arches) and ExHardError (amd64: 30/0 vs 24/6) are BISTABLE and
#   were deliberately left at their banked pessimistic samples — do not re-roll them.
#   (i386 IoDeviceObject bistability re-confirmed directly on 2026-08-02: two back-to-back
#   --smp 2 rounds on IDENTICAL media gave 185/4 then 184/5, the extra one being
#   IoDeviceObject_drv.c:300 STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND. Not an MP-conditional row.)
#   EXPLAINED 2026-10-08: the I/O manager handed DriverEntry an unterminated RegistryPath
#   and IopUnloadDriver queried it as a PWSTR, so :300 depended on the pool bytes after it.
#   Fixed (iomgr-rust driver.rs); IoDeviceObject is 185/4 on every arch, no longer bistable.
# KeSpinLock re-seeded 2026-08-02, 706/79 -> 754/31 — a REAL FIX, not a re-roll.
#   hal-rust's x86 Kx{Acquire,Release}SpinLock were hard-coded UP no-ops (they predate the
#   halmp.dll twin and never learned the `smp` feature), so the kernel stamped owners the
#   HAL never cleared. They now delegate to ntkrnl_sys::inline::ke, the same code ntoskrnl
#   uses. Verified across THREE boots: --smp 1 and both --smp 2 rounds all read 754/31.
#   The 31 residual are upstream's queued-spinlock HACK — no LQ_WAIT bit, and the lock word
#   holds the owner stamp where a real queued lock holds the queue-handle pointer — plus one
#   try-acquire that sets bit 0 without stamping the owner. All present on the UP kernel too
#   (UP is 753/32), so none of them are MP-conditional.
# 2026-10-08, by --write-baseline --only: MmMdl 594 -> 587, equal to the 1-vCPU baseline
#   (its assert count tracks free pages). Not an SMP defect.
